note: All coords in main.webp px (1600x2000). Composite: plate.webp -> shadow01..12 + shadow_floor (RGBA, shadows the units cast on wall/floor) -> units in "order" (farthest from eye level first). plate+shadows+units == main.webp (mean abs err ~0.05/255). Unit layers hold only the pixels visible in the photo (parts of galvanised faces hidden behind the next unit are missing; faces[] polygons give the full un-occluded shapes). Unit faces/corners come from a pinhole camera fitted to the real box geometry (12 x 22.8x101.6x78.7 cm, 22.8 cm gaps), residual <1 px on measured edges. See _wip/cut-minimal/README.md.

camera.world: cm; X along wall to the right from the left edge of the stack, Y up (0 = top of unit01), Z out of the wall (0 = wall plane, 78.7 = front faces). x_img = K (R X + t), K=[[f,0,cx],[0,f,cy],[0,0,1]]; no lens distortion.

match_note: Whaam! (rooms/pop/main.webp, 2400x1015 px) flat colour blocks: after removing lettering, plane/explosion outlines and Ben-Day dots, the remaining flat fields are yellow / red / black / white. For each flat component the largest axis-aligned rectangle with the Judd front-face aspect (w/h=4.21) was found; 12 were picked (largest first; at most 4 red, 4 yellow, 3 black, 1 white; non-overlapping). src_* in pop px, dst_* in minimal px. Order: blocks sorted by source height -> unit01..12 top to bottom. rgb = block colour, dst_rgb = mean lacquer colour of that unit front face (tween target). All candidates: _wip/cut-minimal/whaam_cands.json.

key.desc: overhead gallery light, slightly in front of the wall and a little to the right: each unit throws a dark wedge on the wall directly beneath it (widest near the wall, right of the side face) and the bottom unit a hard-edged parallelogram on the floor just below it

fill.desc: weak soft light from front-right: soft grey shadow strip on the wall to the LEFT of the stack (x~520-640 px)

light.note: estimated by eye from the shadows, world axes as in camera.world; use key for the extrusion shadows
